Docs/Replay/Guide

Replay

Structurally shuffled LZ4 deltas

1 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓

shuffle_lz4_encode combines the schema's byte permutation with the existing LZ4 block codec. A permutation is linear over XOR, so it transforms base XOR target once. Its output is identical to separately shuffling both values and LZ4-encoding their XOR. shuffle_lz4_apply decodes, reverses the permutation and applies the canonical base. Callers still validate the reconstructed target digest and state.

The helpers allocate nothing. Callers supply scratch of at least twice the exact canonical wire size, plus the existing LZ4 workspace for encoding. Scratch may change on failure; the destination and inputs do not. Buffers/workspace must not alias. Rejected sizes, aliases and malformed/truncated blocks preserve output.

The network runner negotiates this candidate separately and retains full, sparse and ordinary LZ4 fallback. It tries the transform only when the existing candidate is at least max(2048, canonical_size / 16) bytes, or no old candidate fits. A transformed candidate must be strictly smaller including its eight-byte transform signature. This heuristic avoids repeatedly testing young, already compact deltas. It does not promise the globally smallest encoding for every possible value.

Scratch is allocated lazily once per server and receiving client, then reused and freed at destruction. It costs twice the canonical snapshot size per such owner; there is no new per-snapshot allocation, retained compression dictionary or changed simulation history. Transforming arrays is lossless: it does not omit old queries, quantize coordinates or change checkpoint semantics.
